shared_context.topic: Blepharitis is a common inflammatory disease of the eyelid margins characterized by chronic inflammation, scaling, and crusting, often causing swelling, burning, itching, or a grainy sensation; it may be associated with rosacea, seborrheic dermatitis, dry eye, chalazion, conjunctivitis, and keratitis, and can be classified as anterior or posterior and acute or chronic.

snippets.output: Blepharitis is a common inflammatory disease of the eyelid margins characterized by chronic inflammation, scaling, and crusting, and it may cause swelling, burning, itching, or a grainy sensation when introducing foreign objects or substances to the eye.
snippets.pattern_notes: Enumerates defining properties and symptoms of blepharitis.

snippets.output: Blepharitis is often associated with systemic diseases, particularly rosacea and seborrheic dermatitis, and with ocular conditions including dry eye, chalazion, conjunctivitis, and keratitis.
snippets.pattern_notes: Enumerates associated systemic and ocular conditions.

snippets.output: Blepharitis can affect any age group.
Blepharitis can be classified by the location of inflammation into anterior and posterior types, and by the duration of symptoms into acute and chronic types.
snippets.pattern_notes: Parallel classification schemes (location, duration) of blepharitis.

snippets.output: The exact pathogenesis of blepharitis is not fully understood, but blepharitis is thought to be caused by bacterial colonization of the eyelids, including Staphylococcus aureus and Staphylococcus epidermidis, as well as meibomian gland dysfunction, allergens, lice affecting the eyelashes, and Demodex folliculorum, a small parasitic mite.
snippets.pattern_notes: Enumerates pathogenesis and causative factors of blepharitis.

snippets.output: Common symptoms of blepharitis include burning sensation, irritation, tearing, photophobia, blurred vision, and red eyes.

Clinical examination of blepharitis reveals scurf, telangiectatic vascular changes of the eyelid margin, inspissated meibomian glands, conjunctival hyperemia, punctuate keratopathy, cornea vascularization, and ulceration.
Blepharitis is diagnosed based on clinical features alone.
Blepharitis is managed with eyelid hygiene and regular cleaning, and sometimes with antimicrobial topical therapy; the form of blepharitis depends on the causative pathogen and underlying cause.
snippets.pattern_notes: Enumerates management properties and dependence on cause.

snippets.output: Blepharitis affects all ages and ethnic groups and has various forms, including seborrheic, staphylococcal, mixed, posterior or meibomitis, and parasitic.
snippets.pattern_notes: Enumerates demographic reach and forms of blepharitis.
